newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ST Aerospace may revisit share structure.
newsitem.headline: ST Aerospace may revisit share structure.

text.p: The question of foreign and local share tranches in Singapore Technologies Aerospace Ltd could be re-opened if its government-owned parent sold down its shareholding, group president Boon Swan Foo said on Monday.
Government-owned Singapore Technologies Pte Ltd (ST) owns 67 percent of ST Aerospace, which, along with other listed ST units, merged its foreign and local share tranches last week.
The aircraft maintenance company has a 49 percent foreign shareholding limit.

But, speaking to reporters after the release of the group's interim results, Boon said the question of a having a foreign share tranche could emerge again if ST decided to sell down its stake in ST Aerospace.

"Moving forward, we would have to find ways and means of solving the problem to make sure this does not repeat itself again. We will have to spend some time looking at how to revisit this issue and resolve it in such a way that nobody gets unhappy," Boon said.
"But we have time on our hand and therefore we will explore and revisit this issue to see what we can do."
Boon said the group's decision to merge its foreign and local share tranches was driven by market forces.
"I have got a lot of feedback from (foreign) investors that they want to invest in ST Aerospace...but they said there is not enough free float. But now there is," he said.
He also said the feedback from shareholders on the decision to merge was positive as local share prices moved up to meet the foreign shares on the day the two tranches merged.
